## Why Execution Is the Moat

```{dot}
//| label: fig-moat-today
//| fig-cap: "Built today: three pillars of defensibility"
//| fig-width: 6
//| fig-height: 2.5
digraph G {
  bgcolor="transparent"
  rankdir=LR
  graph [ranksep=0.5, nodesep=0.5]
  node [style=filled, fillcolor="#1a4a3a", color="#00bc8c",
        fontcolor="#f8f9fa", fontname="Arial", fontsize=10,
        shape=box, width=1.8, height=0.55, margin="0.12,0.08"]
  edge [style=invis]

  A [label="Algorithmic Novelty\nNo competing product\nin this space"]
  B [label="Benchmark Depth\n13 methods × 5 datasets\nfull ablation"]
  C [label="Production Infra\nOne-command runs\nnot notebook code"]

  A -> B -> C
}
```

**Built today:**

- **Algorithmic novelty** — gradient-level shortcut detection is a new direction; no competing product exists
- **Benchmark depth** — 13 methods × 5 datasets × full ablation; hardest comparison set in this subfield
- **Production-grade infra** — one-command reproduction, Optuna search, MLflow tracking

**Compounds over time:**

- First-mover advantage in gradient-based shortcut diagnostics
- Proprietary shortcut taxonomy across domains (built from deployment data)
- Integration partnerships with MLOps platforms
- Enterprise deployment data → feedback loop → better detection

  B2 [label="→ No Lost\nExperiments", fillcolor="#1a4a3a", color="#00bc8c"]

  C1 [label="13 Methods\nCommon Interface", fillcolor="#375a7f"]

  { rank=same; A1; A2 }
  { rank=same; B1; B2 }
  { rank=same; C1; C2 }

| Property | Implementation | Business Value |
|----------|---------------|---------------|
| **Reproducibility** | One-command runs, seed control | Audit trail for compliance |
| **Scalability** | Local / server profiles, SLURM | Laptop to cluster, no rewrite |
| **Tracking** | MLflow + Optuna Bayesian search | No lost experiments |
| **Modularity** | 13 methods, common interface | New methods plug in via 1 function |
| **Documentation** | Quarto site, method docs, guides | Engineer onboarding in days |
